newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares lower, pressured by bonds and lira.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares lower, pressured by bonds and lira.

text.p: Italian shares drifted down to a lower close on Wednesday reflecting weaker domestic bonds and the lira while a lower start to Wall Street saw buying interest from overseas investors largely evaporate, dealers said.

U.S. September consumer price inflation data showed an expected 0.3 percent rise and had little immediate impact, but stocks were unnerved by worries over the European monetary union that knocked domestic bonds and the lira backwards.
The all-share Mibtel ended off 1.12 percent at 9,826 while the blue chip Mib30 of Italy's top listed companies closed down 1.25 percent at 14,808.

The concern over EMU was caused after Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer warned that one-off measures by European nations to reduce budget deficits would not be enough to allow them to join a single European currency.
"This clearly highlighted Italy which is struggling to cut its deficit to qualify for the single currency in 1999," said one share trader in Milan.
Shares had opened slightly higher but soon drifted lower and then dipped after the bonds sell-off and the lira dip.
"After the Italian market has risen so much on EMU hopes, any serious doubts are bound to hurt," said the trader.

Among the blue chips, energy group ENI slipped 1.41 percent to 7,402 lire on talk that the Treasury may increase the size of the second tranche of shares to be offer later this month. This came despite a successful flotation roadshow.
Fiat moved higher at the start after its recent period of weakness, but was pressured lower with the rest of the market and ended off 0.43 percent at 3,981 lire.
Telecoms were generally weak with STET off 1.03 percent at 5,188 lire, TIM down 1.13 percent at 3,229 lire and Telecom Italia down 1.68 percent at 3,343 lire.
